subject.title: [Feature]: Automatic Output Sanitization for Sensitive Data

question: Should OpenClaw define automatic sensitive-value sanitization for final visible agent output as a core security boundary, a plugin/ClawHub capability, or explicitly keep core limited to the current log/tool/transcript redaction surfaces?
rationale: Source inspection shows the requested sanitizer is still absent, but the fix changes user-visible replies and security guarantees, adds or avoids config surface, and may depend on outbound hook guarantees; automation cannot choose that boundary safely.

options.title: Approve a narrow core boundary
options.body: Define scoped core final-output sanitization with defaults, false-positive behavior, reporting, schema/docs/tests, and reuse of the shared redaction engine.

options.title: Route to plugin/ClawHub
options.body: Use message_sending or reply_payload_sending hooks for an optional sanitizer package if maintainers want policy and pattern ownership outside core.

options.title: Keep current redaction boundary
options.body: Declare logs, transcripts, diagnostics, and tool/UI payloads as the supported core redaction surfaces and close or narrow final-output requests accordingly.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow core boundary
recommendation.body: Define scoped core final-output sanitization with defaults, false-positive behavior, reporting, schema/docs/tests, and reuse of the shared redaction engine.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest current history signal across outbound delivery, redaction, and config surfaces involved in the decision.
